original_question: Can the Bikbaev-Tarasov Backlund-transform method be adapted to solve the initial-boundary value problem for the defocusing nonlinear Schrodinger equation i u_t = u_{xx} - 2 |u|^2 u on the half-line with Robin boundary condition u_x(0,t) + q u(0,t) = 0, despite the singularities introduced when the solution is extended from x > 0 to x < 0?
target_in_paper: Problem 5 (initial boundary value problems for integrable systems (IBVP)), specifically the open problem: use the Bikbaev–Tarasov Bäcklund-transform method to solve the half-line Robin problem for the defocusing NLS equation i u_t = u_xx - 2|u|^2 u, where extending the solution from x > 0 to x < 0 creates singularities that must be controlled.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the relevant part of the paper (the Robin-boundary NLS discussion inside Problem 5), the defocusing equation i u_t = u_xx - 2|u|^2 u, the half-line/initial-boundary-value setting, the Robin condition u_x(0,t) + q u(0,t) = 0, the Bikbaev–Tarasov Bäcklund-transform method, and the key obstruction noted in the paper: the extension from x > 0 to x < 0 introduces singularities that must be controlled.
missing_details: The paper formulates this as an open problem inside Problem 5, not as a proved theorem or formal conjecture.
The space-time domain should be made explicit as the quarter-plane x >= 0, t >= 0.
The Robin parameter q is stated to be fixed.
To make the IBVP stand alone, it helps to mention prescribed initial data u(x,0) = f(x) on x >= 0; the exact open-problem sentence assumes the usual IBVP data from the nearby context.

The paper’s nearby context explains that the Bikbaev–Tarasov method is a nonlinear method of images: it extends the half-line solution to x < 0 by a Bäcklund transformation so that the problem becomes a whole-line problem.
The paper also notes that, in the defocusing case, the long-time behavior should be very different from the focusing case; this motivation is implicit in your draft but not stated.

Your draft should avoid absorbing the neighboring but distinct open problem about proving classical smoothness for Robin IBVPs and more general nonlinearities; that is a separate question in the paper.

The paper does not specify a sharper function-space class for the initial data in this exact open-problem sentence, so a paper-faithful rewrite should not add extra Sobolev/Schwartz hypotheses on its own.
refined_question: Can one use the Bikbaev–Tarasov Bäcklund-transformation method to solve, on the quarter-plane x >= 0, t >= 0, the initial-boundary value problem for the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation i u_t = u_xx - 2|u|^2 u with prescribed initial data u(x,0) = f(x) on x >= 0 and fixed Robin boundary condition u_x(0,t) + q u(0,t) = 0, by extending the solution from x > 0 to x < 0 and controlling the singularities created by that extension?
justification: The draft clearly targets the first Robin-boundary open problem in Problem 5 of Deift’s survey. The paper’s official formulation is the sentence on using the Bikbaev–Tarasov method for the defocusing NLS Robin IBVP; the surrounding context supplies the quarter-plane setting for NLS IBVPs, the Robin condition with fixed q, the interpretation of the method as a nonlinear method of images via Bäcklund extension to the whole line, and the specific obstacle that singularities appear in the defocusing extension. The later discussion about classical smoothness for Robin problems is a separate neighboring open problem and should not be merged into this one.
